memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'The priests must not desecrate the sacred offerings the Israelites
present to the LORD by allowing them to eat the sacred offerings and
so bring upon them guilt requiring payment. I am the LORD, who makes
them holy'" - Lev 22:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The responsibility here falls on the priests, not on the ordinary
Israelite. If a priest was careless and let someone eat what they
should not have, he brought guilt on that person. His carelessness
cost somebody else.

That is a weighty thought. Our carelessness rarely stays neatly within
our own lives. A leader's casual attitude teaches a whole congregation.
A parent's indifference shapes a child's view of God for decades. A
friend's flippant advice can send someone down a painful road.

James warns that not many should become teachers, because they will be
judged more strictly (Jas 3:1). Jesus spoke sternly about causing
little ones to stumble (Matt 18:6). Paul was willing to limit his own
freedom rather than damage a weaker brother's conscience (Rom 14:13).

Dear friend, this is not meant to make you fearful of influence. It is
meant to make you thoughtful about it. You have more influence than you
think - in your home, your workplace, your church group, your online
words.

And once more the chapter reminds us where holiness comes from: "I am
the LORD, who makes them holy." Ask Him to make you a safe person for
others to be around.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who is watching my life more closely than I realise?
2. Has my casualness ever made it easier for someone else to stumble?
3. Where should I limit my freedom for someone else's good?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, make me careful with the influence You have given me. Let my
life help others toward You and never trip them up. Amen.
